result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.panther_vector_similarity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Find the nodes most similar to a source node by comparing their Panther profiles. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.panther_vector_similarity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Find the nodes most similar to a source node by comparing their Panther profiles. title: >- [Graph.panther_vector_similarity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Find the nodes most similar to a source node by comparing their Panther profiles. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the nodes most similar to a source node by comparing their Panther profiles. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L29507-L29649){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.panther_vector_similarity( source, D=10, k=5, path_length=5, c=0.5, delta=0.1, epsilon=None, weighted=None, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Panther vector similarity](../assets/graphs/panther-vector-similarity.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same two triangles joined by the bridge c to x, with source a outlined. Panther++ describes each node by its top random-path similarities, sorted, and compares those profiles, so it finds nodes in the same structural position rather than nearby ones. The k = 3 most similar nodes, in the accent color with their scores as badges, are b (349.7), y (39.1) and z (38.7): like a, each sits on a triangle away from the bridge, and b, a's twin, scores far highest. panther_similarity instead ranks c, b and x, a's neighbors." width="100%"} Panther++ (Zhang et al., 2015) extends `panther_similarity()`: instead of asking how often two nodes share random paths, it gives every node a feature vector of its `D` largest Panther scores (against any node, itself included) and compares those vectors. Two nodes are similar when their neighborhoods look alike, even if they are far apart and never share a path, so it captures structural roles, such as the leaves of different stars or the hubs of different communities, much as role-based embeddings do. The scores are estimates; pass `seed=` for repeatable results. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node to compare against, as an ID or label. [D]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The length of each node's feature vector: how many of its largest Panther scores to keep. At most the number of non-isolated nodes. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[5]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How many of the most similar nodes to return. [path_length]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[5]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The number of steps in each random path ($T$), at least 2. [c]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.5]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A positive constant that scales the number of sampled paths. [delta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The probability, between 0 and 1, that the Panther scores miss the `epsilon=` error bound. [epsilon]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The error bound on the Panther scores, which sets how many paths are sampled. If `None` (default), $\sqrt{1 / |E|}$. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights for the random steps. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag; edges without a weight count as `1.0`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Up to `k` node IDs (never `source`) with their scores, from most to least similar (ties in node ID order). A score is $1 / d$ for the Euclidean distance $d$ between the two feature vectors, so it has no upper bound; a node whose vector equals the source's scores $1 / \epsilon_{\text{mach}} \approx 4.5 \times 10^{15}$. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `source` doesn't exist or is isolated, `D` is not a positive integer or exceeds the number of non-isolated nodes, another parameter is out of range, a weight is negative, or (in a directed graph) a path reaches a node with no out-edges. ::: ## Warns {.doc-warns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [UserWarning]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `k` is more than the number of other non-isolated nodes, all of which are returned. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The paths are sampled exactly as in `panther_similarity()`, after dropping isolated nodes. Node $v$'s vector $\theta_v$ holds its `D` largest scores $s(v, u)$ (the share of paths holding both $v$ and $u$, with $s(v, v)$ the share holding $v$) in descending order, padded with zeros when $v$ shares paths with fewer than `D` nodes. The similarity is the paper's $1 / \lVert \theta_v - \theta_s \rVert$, with the distance clamped to machine epsilon so equal vectors don't divide by zero. Co-occurrences are counted sparsely, so the cost is about $O(R T^2 + V \log V)$ for $R$ sampled paths. The unnormalized scores follow the fix in NetworkX pull request #8578; NetworkX releases without it clamp the distance to `epsilon` and rescale the scores to at most 1. NetworkX's `panther_vector_similarity` also raises an error when `k` exceeds the number of nodes, and finds the nearest vectors with a k-d tree (ties in arbitrary order); its random paths come from a different generator, so the scores agree only statistically. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a star, the leaves all look alike, so the other leaves get equal, high scores against a leaf, though no path joins two leaves without passing through the center: ::: {#fe4b27b6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec star = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(20, label=False) star.panther_vector_similarity(2, k=3, seed=1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {14: 39.83716857408422, 17: 39.83716857408422, 6: 39.83716857408417} ``` ::: ::: Two triangles joined by a bridge. With a tight `epsilon=` (and so many sampled paths), `a` matches its triangle twin `b` best, then `y` and `z`, which hold the same place in the other triangle, while the bridge ends `c` and `x` score far lower: ::: {#4963a03e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["a", "b", "c", "x", "y", "z"]) graph.add_edges( [("a", "b"), ("b", "c"), ("c", "a"), ("c", "x"), ("x", "y"), ("y", "z"), ("z", "x")] ) scores = graph.panther_vector_similarity("a", D=4, epsilon=0.05, seed=1) {graph.get_label_from_id(n): round(s, 3) for n, s in scores.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'b': 349.736, 'y': 39.073, 'z': 38.719, 'c': 3.261, 'x': 3.201} ``` ::: :::
